title: Stalks of $\mathcal J\mathcal F$, of $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ and of powers of an ideal sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of ideals (a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal O_X$) and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal J\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, $a\otimes s\mapsto as$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal J\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$, and $\mathcal J^1=\mathcal J$, $\mathcal J^{n+1}=\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal J^n$ (the product just defined, with $\mathcal F=\mathcal J^n$, a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of $\mathcal O_X$). Let $x\in X$, with stalks and germs as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then: (1) the stalk map $\mathcal J_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ of the inclusion is injective, so $\mathcal J_x$ is identified with an ideal of the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$; likewise $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is injective; (2) under this identification $(\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x=\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x$, the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-submodule of $\mathcal F_x$ generated by the products $a\,m$, $a\in\mathcal J_x$, $m\in\mathcal F_x$; (3) the stalk at $x$ of the quotient map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F$ induces an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules $\mathcal F_x/\mathcal J_x\mathcal F_x\cong(\mathcal F/\mathcal J\mathcal F)_x$; (4) for every $n\ge1$, $(\mathcal J^n)_x=(\mathcal J_x)^n$ as ideals of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $(\mathcal J^n\mathcal F)_x=(\mathcal J_x)^n\mathcal F_x$ as submodules of $\mathcal F_x$, and $(\mathcal F/\mathcal J^n\mathcal F)_x\cong\mathcal F_x/(\mathcal J_x)^n\mathcal F_x$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AG (lemma-abelian: a complex of O_X-modules is exact iff it is exact on all stalks; kernels, images and cokernels are computed stalkwise) and Lemma 01CB (lemma-stalk-tensor-product: (F tensor G)_x = F_x tensor G_x); the statement combines them and is used without proof in Stacks, Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (coherent.tex, lemma-systems-with-proper-support)

proof.text: Construct the unit-stalk identification using preservation of filtered colimits by forgetful functors from commutative rings to abelian groups. The comparison sends every module germ to its ring germ. Its additivity is automatic; represent a scalar and a vector on a common neighbourhood to prove linearity.

Use module_stalk_exact clause (1) and sectionwise injectivity of a sheaf mono to prove stalk injectivity for iota and for every categorical image inclusion. Apply the multiplication-range lemma to identify the product inclusion range with I times F_x.

By module_stalk_exact clause (3), the stalk cokernel projection is surjective with kernel equal to the product inclusion range. Mathlib quotEquivOfEq and quotKerEquivOfSurjective give the quotient equivalence with the required formula on quotient representatives.

Induct on the positive exponent n=1+k. For n=1 the ideal range is I. At the successor, apply the multiplication-range lemma with F=J^n and map its range along the inclusion of J^n into the unit stalk. LinearMap.range_comp and Submodule.map_smul'' identify the result with I times I^n, equal to I^(n+1). Apply the same range lemma and quotient construction to J^n and the arbitrary F to conclude the final two clauses.

proof_origin.place: 01AG and 01CB, combined as in the proof of 0CYV; Lean reduction B3 proves unit comparison, injectivity, quotients and positive-power induction, with multiplication range split off.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (clauses (1)-(4) checked; true for any ringed space). Proof written in five steps: (1) injectivity of stalks of sub-O_X-modules, J_x as an ideal; the multiplication map mu: J (x) F -> F and its stalk, identified via the existing 01CB node lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-tensor (unit sk-thm-reduction, used as a generic tool lemma) with alpha (x) m -> alpha m; (2) (JF)_x = image of mu_x = J_x F_x; (3) F_x/J_xF_x = (F/JF)_x from stalks of cokernels; (4) induction on n for J^n, applying (1)-(3) to the ideal sheaf J^n. Stalk exactness of O_X-modules (Stacks 01AG with the text before it) had no node: created lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact (unsplit; Mathlib has only the abelian-sheaf case, TopCat.Sheaf.exact_iff_stalkFunctor_map_exact, and SheafOfModules.toSheaf preserving finite limits, not cokernels). Proof origin agent: the combination is stated without proof in 0CYV and 01CB's proof is omitted in Stacks.
